emily (oncall): :rotating_light: customer reports spike of 502s and timeouts hitting hosted inference in az-eastus1, starting ~09:10 UTC
alex (support): Which customers? Getting multiple tickets: app-zenith and quickwrite both reporting elevated 5xx and long tail latencies
maria (csm): app-zenith on a paid Dedicated->Hosted hybrid, they saw retry storms and billing noise. Customer demanding RCA and mitigation ASAP
emily (oncall): I can see gateway 502s in our edge logs for eastus1-azB: snippet: "gateway=api-gw eastus1-azB 502 backend_conn_reset seq=xxx retransmit=high"
raj (neteng): Seeing packet dup/retx on the edge-to-transit link from eastus1-azB -> LambdaTransit (provider). BGP shows AS path changes and withdraws around 09:08-09:12 UTC. bgp-monitor-bot: "ASPATH changed: 64512 -> 64499 -> 64512 flapping"
emily (oncall): Can you confirm whether it's asymmetric routing or partial blackhole? Symptoms: repeated TCP 3-way + dup acks then RSTs, clients retrying and gateway returning 502s
raj (neteng): Run on-box `mtr -c 50 -r -w 1.2.3.4` from edge and `tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp and (port 443)'` to capture dup acks. I'll correlate with transit-side taps
alex (support): I've asked customers for X-Request-Id and sample request payloads. Also asked for `curl -v -H "x-request-id: <id>"` to reproduce. app-zenith provided id: req-zoe-1122
emily (oncall): Quick repro from our side with that id: `curl -i -H "x-request-id: req-zoe-1122" https://api.redwood.run/v1/generate` -> intermittent `502 Bad Gateway` and long `FIN,ACK` resets
raj (neteng): Captures show ECMP path flip with one path introducing 20-30% packet reorder and duplication. TCP stack on our edge closes backend connections after repeated retransmits -> 502s. Provider admitting microsecond-level optics flaps on one fiber pair
emily (oncall): Impact scope? Which AZs/regions and % errors?
raj (neteng): Affected: eastus1-azB primarily, some cross-az affected because smart-router was still preferring azB paths for a subset of customers -> ~12% 5xx increase for hosted inference in region, error spike from 09:07-09:22 UTC
maria (csm): Noted customer concern: billing spikes due to automatic retries. CSMs asked for immediate mitigations and crediting plan
emily (oncall): Mitigation steps enacted: 1) Temporarily increased routing preference away from the affected transit peer for azB (fail traffic to azA/azC); 2) Enabled stricter connection hold/retry window on gateway to reduce duplicate billing retries; 3) Opened ticket with LambdaTransit (Tkt# LT-94821) and escalated to their NOC
raj (neteng): Also pushed hotfix to smart-router to avoid preferring failing ECMP path for new flows (change `ecmp_min_success=3 -> 5`), rolling to azB now
sre-bot: deploy-bot:hotfix succeeded on eastus1-azB (canary 3/3) :white_check_mark:
emily (oncall): Post-mitigation metrics show 5xx drop back to baseline within 12 minutes of failover. We're still monitoring for flaps
alex (support): Messaging to customers drafted: apologized, root cause summary, mitigation, and proposed credit. Waiting on legal signoff before sending to enterprise customers
maria (csm): App-zenith confirmed degraded but stable, requested postmortem and confirmation that retry billing will be reviewed
emily (oncall): Follow-ups: (1) collect all tcpdump/mtr/traces and attach to LT ticket, (2) schedule a follow-up call with LambdaTransit NOC, (3) run BGP dampening defaults review and consider automated reroute thresholds, (4) draft postmortem for incidents channel
raj (neteng): Quick note: recommend we add a small prefix-based preference override for critical enterprise customers to avoid cross-az preference flips during provider instability
emily (oncall): Agreed. I'll start the postmortem doc. tagging @raj @alex to add logs + timeline. :thumbsup:
bgp-monitor-bot: alert cleared for eastus1-azB (AS path stabilized)
emily (oncall): Closing thread for now, will update once provider confirms root cause and credits secured
alex (support): Thanks team, will keep customers informed and update billing queue
